Algebra I · Lesson 9.1

Meet the Quadratic

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Chapter 8 ended with a promise, that x2+7x+12x2+7x+12 equals (x+3)(x+4)(x+3)(x+4). Multiply to check. (x+3)(x+4)=x(x+4)+3(x+4)=x2+4x+3x+12=x2+7x+12(x+3)(x+4)=x(x+4)+3(x+4)=x2+4x+3x+12=x2+7x+12, so the promise holds. An expression ax2+bx+cax2+bx+c with aa not zero is a quadratic. This lesson multiplies linear factors into quadratics. Reversing that is the next lesson's job.

Problem
Multiply (x+5)(x+6)(x+5)(x+6) the way the opener multiplied its product, splitting the first factor and distributing each part over the second. Collect like terms and enter the coefficient of xx.
Show a hint
  • Write the product as x(x+6)+5(x+6)x(x+6)+5(x+6). That is chapter 2's distributive property with the whole factor (x+6)(x+6) as the multiplier.
  • Each part distributes again, four products in all. Two of them contain xx to the first power, and those two collect.
Show the full solution
(x+5)(x+6)=x(x+6)+5(x+6)=x2+6x+5x+30=x2+11x+30(x+5)(x+6)=x(x+6)+5(x+6)=x2+6x+5x+30=x2+11x+30, so the coefficient of xx is 1111​. The two cross products 6x6x and 5x5x are like terms, and collecting them is where the middle term of every such product comes from.
Problem
Expand (x+10)(x−2)(x+10)(x−2), keeping the minus sign with the 22 in both products that use it. Enter the constant term of the result.
Show a hint
  • Split as x(x−2)+10(x−2)x(x−2)+10(x−2) and distribute each part. Two of the four products come out negative.
  • The constant term is the product of the two constants, +10+10 and −2−2, sign included.
Show the full solution
(x+10)(x−2)=x2−2x+10x−20=x2+8x−20(x+10)(x−2)=x2−2x+10x−20=x2+8x−20, so the constant term is −20−20​. The only constant is 10⋅(−2)10⋅(−2), negative because exactly one of the two constants is negative.
Key idea
Distribute twice. (x+r)(x+s)=x(x+s)+r(x+s)(x+r)(x+s)=x(x+s)+r(x+s), the whole second factor treated as a single multiplier, and then each part is distributed again, x2+sx+rx+rsx2+sx+rx+rs. Four products in all, every term of the first factor times every term of the second, then like terms are collected. Nothing here is new. Chapter 2's distributive property is used twice, once with (x+s)(x+s) as the multiplier and once inside each part, and the same two steps apply unchanged for any signs and for any coefficients on xx.
Problem
Expand (x−5)(x−8)(x−5)(x−8). Both constants are negative this time, so all four sign decisions in the four products matter. Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show a hint
  • Split as x(x−8)−5(x−8)x(x−8)−5(x−8) and distribute each part, keeping every sign.
  • The two cross products are −8x−8x and −5x−5x. The last product, (−5)(−8)(−5)(−8), is positive.
Show the full solution
(x−5)(x−8)=x2−8x−5x+40=x2−13x+40(x−5)(x−8)=x2−8x−5x+40=x2−13x+40, so the coefficient of xx is −13−13​. Both cross products are negative and add, while the constant (−5)(−8)=40(−5)(−8)=40 comes out positive.
Problem
Expand (8x−5)(2x+9)(8x−5)(2x+9). The x2x2 coefficient is now a product of two numbers, and two of the four products contain xx to the first power. Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show a hint
  • Distribute twice as before, 8x(2x+9)−5(2x+9)8x(2x+9)−5(2x+9), and write all four products before collecting anything.
  • The two xx products come from 8x⋅98x⋅9 and −5⋅2x−5⋅2x. Compute both, signs included, then add.
Show the full solution
(8x−5)(2x+9)=16x2+72x−10x−45=16x2+62x−45(8x−5)(2x+9)=16x2+72x−10x−45=16x2+62x−45, so the coefficient of xx is 6262​. With leading coefficients the middle is no longer a plain sum of the two constants, it is 72−1072−10, one cross product at a time.
Key idea
The forward pattern. (x+r)(x+s)=x2+(r+s)x+rs(x+r)(x+s)=x2+(r+s)x+rs. The two cross products are sxsx and rxrx, like terms, so the middle coefficient is the sum r+sr+s and the constant is the product rsrs. Check the first problem, 5+6=115+6=11 and 5⋅6=305⋅6=30. The pattern holds for any signs, but only when the x2x2 coefficient is 11. With leading coefficients the middle was 72x−10x72x−10x, one cross product at a time, not a plain sum. This is a fact about multiplying. Recovering rr and ss from an expansion is the next lesson's work.

A few products come up so often they are worth knowing on sight, a sum squared, a difference squared, and a sum times the matching difference. Squaring means multiplying by itself, so (x+k)2(x+k)2 means (x+k)(x+k)(x+k)(x+k), four products again, and it is not x2+k2x2+k2. The next two problems work out two of these, and the third follows the same way.

Problem
Write (x+8)2(x+8)2 as (x+8)(x+8)(x+8)(x+8), the square written out as the product it abbreviates, and expand it with the same double distribution as every product so far. Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show a hint
  • Squaring means multiplying by itself, so the same double distribution applies, four products again.
  • The cross product is 8x8x both times, and the two copies are like terms.
Show the full solution
(x+8)2=(x+8)(x+8)=x2+8x+8x+64=x2+16x+64(x+8)2=(x+8)(x+8)=x2+8x+8x+64=x2+16x+64, so the coefficient of xx is 1616​. The cross product appears twice, which is why the answer is 1616 and not 88, and why (x+8)2(x+8)2 is not x2+64x2+64.
Problem
Compute 61×5961×59 without a calculator by writing it as (60+1)(60−1)(60+1)(60−1) and expanding all four products. Enter the product.
Show a hint
  • The four products are 60⋅6060⋅60, 60⋅(−1)60⋅(−1), 1⋅601⋅60, and 1⋅(−1)1⋅(−1). Two of them cancel.
  • The cross products are −60−60 and +60+60, so they add to zero. You are left with one square minus a much smaller square.
Show the full solution
61×59=(60+1)(60−1)=3600−60+60−1=3600−1=359961×59=(60+1)(60−1)=3600−60+60−1=3600−1=3599​. The cross products cancel whenever the two factors are the same distance from a round number, one above and one below, which is what makes this a mental calculation.
Key idea
Three named identities. (a+b)2=a2+2ab+b2(a+b)2=a2+2ab+b2, (a−b)2=a2−2ab+b2(a−b)2=a2−2ab+b2, and (a+b)(a−b)=a2−b2(a+b)(a−b)=a2−b2, the difference of squares. Each one is the same double distribution. The difference square is (a−b)(a−b)=a2−ab−ab+b2(a−b)(a−b)=a2−ab−ab+b2, the cross product −ab−ab twice, and the sum square is the same with +ab+ab, the source of the 1616 in (x+8)2(x+8)2. In the conjugate product the cross products are opposite and cancel, which is why 61×5961×59 reduced to 3600−13600−1. The middle term of a square is 2ab2ab, not abab, and a middle term is missing only in the conjugate product.

An expansion is a claim that the two sides are equal at every value of xx, so they must agree at any value you try. At x=10x=10, (x+1)(x+8)(x+1)(x+8) is 11⋅18=19811⋅18=198, and x2+9x+8x2+9x+8 is 100+90+8=198100+90+8=198. At x=0x=0 only the constant term is left, so pick a nonzero value. Agreement at one value is strong evidence. A disagreement proves an error.

Problem
A student expands (x+6)(x+9)(x+6)(x+9) and writes x2+14x+54x2+14x+54. Substitute x=10x=10 into the product and into the claim to confirm they disagree, then enter the correct coefficient of xx.
Show a hint
  • At x=10x=10 the product is 16⋅1916⋅19. Evaluate the claim at 1010 as well and compare.
  • The constant 5454 is correct, since 6⋅9=546⋅9=54. Recompute the two cross products, 9x9x and 6x6x.
Show the full solution
At x=10x=10 the product is 16⋅19=30416⋅19=304 while the claim gives 100+140+54=294100+140+54=294, so the claim is wrong. Expanding correctly, (x+6)(x+9)=x2+9x+6x+54=x2+15x+54(x+6)(x+9)=x2+9x+6x+54=x2+15x+54, and the coefficient of xx is 1515​. The gap between 304304 and 294294 is 1010, exactly one missing xx at x=10x=10.
Fun fact
The acronym FOIL, First Outer Inner Last, first appeared in William Betz's 1929 textbook Algebra for Today. The label is centuries younger than the method, and the method needs no acronym, it is the distributive property used twice.
Problem
Expand (x−10y)(x+8y)(x−10y)(x+8y). The same rule applies, every term of the first factor times every term of the second, with two letters to track. Enter the coefficient of xyxy.
Show a hint
  • Four products again, x⋅xx⋅x, x⋅8yx⋅8y, −10y⋅x−10y⋅x, and −10y⋅8y−10y⋅8y. Two of them contain both letters.
  • Collect 8xy8xy and −10xy−10xy. The y2y2 product is separate and is not the answer.
Show the full solution
(x−10y)(x+8y)=x2+8xy−10xy−80y2=x2−2xy−80y2(x−10y)(x+8y)=x2+8xy−10xy−80y2=x2−2xy−80y2, so the coefficient of xyxy is −2−2​. The xyxy coefficient is the collected sum 8−108−10, while −80−80 is the y2y2 coefficient, the product.
Key idea
The zero product property. If a product of two numbers is zero, then at least one of the numbers is zero. The reason is short. The product of two nonzero numbers is never zero, so if a product is zero there is no other possibility. The consequence is the whole point of factored form. An equation with a product on one side and zero on the other splits into separate linear equations, one for each factor, and solving linear equations is chapter 4's work.

The payoff is immediate. In (x−6)(x+10)=0(x−6)(x+10)=0 a product equals zero, so at least one factor is zero, and each factor gives a chapter 4 equation. x−6=0x−6=0 gives x=6x=6, and x+10=0x+10=0 gives x=−10x=−10, the sign flipped. Of the two, 66 is the larger, since −10−10 is negative. A factor can also be xx itself, and x=0x=0 is already solved.

Problem
Solve (x−8)(x+15)=0(x−8)(x+15)=0. The left side is zero exactly when one of the factors is zero. Enter the larger of the two solutions.
Show a hint
  • Set each factor equal to zero and solve the two linear equations separately.
  • x+15=0x+15=0 is solved by a negative number. Compare the two solutions on the number line before choosing the larger.
Show the full solution
x−8=0x−8=0 gives x=8x=8 and x+15=0x+15=0 gives x=−15x=−15, so the larger solution is 88​. The factor x+15x+15 is zero at −15−15, not 1515, and 8>−158>−15 even though 1515 is bigger than 88.
Problem
The left side of x(x−16)=0x(x−16)=0 has xx itself as a factor. Count every value of xx that makes the left side zero, then enter the number of solutions of the equation.
Show a hint
  • The zero product property applies to any two factors. Set each of the two factors equal to zero.
  • The equation x=0x=0 is already solved, and its solution counts.
Show the full solution
The factors are xx and x−16x−16, so x=0x=0 or x=16x=16, and the number of solutions is 22​. Dropping x=0x=0 is the common error, but zero is a solution, since substituting it back gives 0⋅(0−16)=00⋅(0−16)=0.
Key idea
At most two solutions. Each linear factor is zero at one number, so two factors give at most two solutions, and a repeated factor like (x−k)2=0(x−k)2=0 gives exactly one, since both factors are zero at the same number. The property also has a boundary. (x−a)(x−b)=10(x−a)(x−b)=10 determines neither factor, because two numbers can multiply to 1010 in endless ways, 2⋅52⋅5, 20⋅1220⋅21​, and on forever. Only a zero product forces a factor to be zero, so before any splitting the equation must have zero on one side.

Multiplying two binomials is now mechanical, four products and a collection, the same every time. The chapter's prize is the reverse direction, starting from x2+bx+cx2+bx+c and recovering the factors, because the zero product property applies only to factored form. That reversal starts in the next lesson.

Problem
Solve (10x−25)(2x+1)=0(10x−25)(2x+1)=0. Each factor is zero at its own value of xx, and neither value is an integer this time. Enter the positive solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Each factor gives one linear equation, 10x−25=010x−25=0 and 2x+1=02x+1=0. Solve both.
  • One solution is negative. The other comes out as a fraction that is not yet in lowest terms, so reduce it before entering.
Show the full solution
10x−25=010x−25=0 gives x=2510=52x=1025​=25​, and 2x+1=02x+1=0 gives x=−12x=−21​, so the positive solution is 5225​​. Lowest terms means dividing out the common factor of 2525 and 1010, which is 55.
Problem
There is one value of bb for which 36x2+bx+12136x2+bx+121 is exactly the square (6x−11)2(6x−11)2. Expand the square and compare the two expressions term by term. Enter bb.
Show a hint
  • Use the square-of-a-difference identity with 6x6x as the first term and 1111 as the second.
  • The middle term of the expansion is −2⋅6x⋅11−2⋅6x⋅11. Match it against bxbx.
Show the full solution
(6x−11)2=36x2−2⋅6⋅11 x+121=36x2−132x+121(6x−11)2=36x2−2⋅6⋅11x+121=36x2−132x+121, so matching middle terms gives b=−132b=−132​. The standard misses are −66−66, forgetting the 22 in 2ab2ab, and +132+132, dropping the sign of the subtraction.

Every product (x+r)(x+s)(x+r)(x+s) expands to x2+(r+s)x+rsx2+(r+s)x+rs, the sum in the middle and the product at the end. Lesson 9.2, Factoring x2+bx+cx2+bx+c, starts from the expanded form and recovers rr and ss, a search with exactly two clues, the sum and the product.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Expand (x+1)(x+9)(x+1)(x+9). Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show the solution
(x+1)(x+9)=x2+9x+x+9=x2+10x+9(x+1)(x+9)=x2+9x+x+9=x2+10x+9, so the coefficient of xx is 1010​.
Practice
Expand (x−1)(x+14)(x−1)(x+14). Enter the constant term.
Show the solution
(x−1)(x+14)=x2+14x−x−14=x2+13x−14(x−1)(x+14)=x2+14x−x−14=x2+13x−14, so the constant term is −14−14​. The sign comes from (−1)⋅14(−1)⋅14, one negative constant.
Practice
Expand (x−2)(x−9)(x−2)(x−9). Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show the solution
(x−2)(x−9)=x2−9x−2x+18=x2−11x+18(x−2)(x−9)=x2−9x−2x+18=x2−11x+18, so the coefficient of xx is −11−11​. Two negative constants give a negative middle and a positive constant.
Practice
Expand (2x+1)(5x+8)(2x+1)(5x+8). Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show the solution
(2x+1)(5x+8)=10x2+16x+5x+8=10x2+21x+8(2x+1)(5x+8)=10x2+16x+5x+8=10x2+21x+8, so the coefficient of xx is 2121​.
Practice
Expand (x+11)2(x+11)2. Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show the solution
(x+11)2=x2+2⋅11x+121=x2+22x+121(x+11)2=x2+2⋅11x+121=x2+22x+121, so the coefficient of xx is 2222​. The middle is 2ab2ab, not abab, because the cross product appears twice.
Practice
Expand (x−10)2(x−10)2. Enter the constant term.
Show the solution
(x−10)2=x2−20x+100(x−10)2=x2−20x+100, so the constant term is 100100​. The constant of a square is always positive, only the middle term carries the minus.
Practice
Compute 85×7585×75 in your head by writing it as (80+5)(80−5)(80+5)(80−5). Enter the product.
Show the solution
85×75=(80+5)(80−5)=6400−25=637585×75=(80+5)(80−5)=6400−25=6375​. The cross products, +400+400 and −400−400, cancel, so only 802−52802−52 is left.
Practice
Expand (x+20)(x−20)(x+20)(x−20). Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show the solution
(x+20)(x−20)=x2−20x+20x−400=x2−400(x+20)(x−20)=x2−20x+20x−400=x2−400, so the coefficient of xx is 00​. The expansion has no xx term at all, which is the difference of squares pattern.
Practice
Expand (2x−9)(8x−1)(2x−9)(8x−1). Enter the coefficient of xx.
Show the solution
(2x−9)(8x−1)=16x2−2x−72x+9=16x2−74x+9(2x−9)(8x−1)=16x2−2x−72x+9=16x2−74x+9, so the coefficient of xx is −74−74​. The constant (−9)(−1)=9(−9)(−1)=9 is positive while both cross products are negative.
Practice
A student expands (x+6)(x+10)(x+6)(x+10) and writes x2+16x+66x2+16x+66. Substitute x=5x=5 into the product and into the claim to see they disagree, then enter the correct constant term.
Show the solution
At x=5x=5 the product is 11⋅15=16511⋅15=165 while the claim gives 25+80+66=17125+80+66=171, so the claim is wrong. The constant is 6⋅10=606⋅10=60, so the correct constant term is 6060​. A check at x=0x=0 would have caught this even faster, since substituting x=0x=0 leaves only the constant term.
Practice
Expand (x−6y)(x+15y)(x−6y)(x+15y). Enter the coefficient of xyxy.
Show the solution
(x−6y)(x+15y)=x2+15xy−6xy−90y2=x2+9xy−90y2(x−6y)(x+15y)=x2+15xy−6xy−90y2=x2+9xy−90y2, so the coefficient of xyxy is 99​.
Practice
Solve (x−13)(x+6)=0(x−13)(x+6)=0. Enter the larger solution.
Show the solution
x−13=0x−13=0 gives x=13x=13 and x+6=0x+6=0 gives x=−6x=−6, so the larger solution is 1313​.
Practice
Solve (x+16)(x+21)=0(x+16)(x+21)=0. Both solutions are negative. Enter the larger one.
Show the solution
The solutions are x=−16x=−16 and x=−21x=−21, and −16>−21−16>−21, so the larger solution is −16−16​. Larger means further right on the number line, not bigger digits.
Practice
Solve x(2x−15)=0x(2x−15)=0. Enter the positive solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
x=0x=0 or 2x−15=02x−15=0, which gives x=152x=215​, so the positive solution is 152215​​. Zero is a solution too, just not the positive one.
Practice
How many solutions does (x−17)2=0(x−17)2=0 have? Enter the count.
Show the solution
Both factors are x−17x−17, so the only solution is x=17x=17, and the count is 11​. A repeated factor gives one solution, not two, since both linear equations are the same.
Practice
To solve (x−1)(x+13)=10(x−1)(x+13)=10, Mara sets x−1=10x−1=10 and answers x=11x=11. Evaluate (x−1)(x+13)(x−1)(x+13) at x=11x=11. Enter the value you get.
Show the solution
At x=11x=11 the factors are 1010 and 2424, so (x−1)(x+13)=10⋅24=240(x−1)(x+13)=10⋅24=240​. Many pairs of numbers multiply to 1010, so x−1=10x−1=10 was only a guess. Splitting an equation factor by factor is valid only when the other side is 00.
Practice
Find the value of bb that makes 81x2+bx+2581x2+bx+25 exactly (9x−5)2(9x−5)2.
Show the solution
(9x−5)2=81x2−2⋅9⋅5 x+25=81x2−90x+25(9x−5)2=81x2−2⋅9⋅5x+25=81x2−90x+25, so b=−90b=−90​. Forgetting the factor 22 gives −45−45, and dropping the subtraction's sign gives +90+90, the two standard misses.
